title: Deadly Cure
subtitle: Only those with nothing to drink would sip from a poisoned well.

items.text: The sky grows dim above them. A low, haunting chant drifts up into the air. Curious, Mayfly looks toward the end of the street.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Oh, right, the parade's coming.
A crowded wave of people surges into view from the distance. Mayfly cranes her neck, straining to see.

items.speaker: Chant
items.text: Withered grass devours bone. On icy plain the spirits moan.

items.speaker: Chant
items.text: When the city falls, the Immortal descends. Longevity granted, no death, no end.
The unearthly parade advances; a line of towering figures leads its approach in long, otherworldly strides. It takes a moment to spot the stilts as they push against the fabric with each step.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What are they singing?

items.speaker: Woman I
items.text: Withered grass devours bone. On icy plain the spirits moan.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What is ...
The parade is near. Their chanting pours over Mayfly like a flood of divine music.

items.speaker: "Immortal" I
items.text: When the city falls, the Immortal descends. Longevity granted, no death, no end.

items.speaker: All
items.text: When the city falls, the Immortal descends. Longevity granted, no death, no end.
A fox and a woman have appeared over Mayfly's shoulder. Their hushed voices brushing against her ear.

items.speaker: Woman I
items.text: We sit at the bottom of society, but still, we deserve dignity. One Yao's voice may not be heard, but what of a hundred or even a thousand more?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: W-Who are you? What do you want?

items.speaker: Fox
items.text: Same as you, we are Yao.

items.speaker: Fox
items.text: You've seen them bat us off, even kill us, haven't you? Will you continue to suffer in silence? Will you live on in fear?

items.speaker: Woman I
items.text: We need to fight. Fight for our lives! Save our people and claim the Method of Longevity for our own! Overthrow humans and rule the world!

items.speaker: Fox
items.text: Come, join us! If we are doomed, then we will doom them with us!

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: No. I-I ...
She looks around, hoping to find help, only to realize she is surrounded by thick billows of scented fog.

items.speaker: Woman I
items.text: Those that are not with us are the enemy.

items.speaker: Woman I
items.text: Did they ever show you mercy? Then, why hesitate?
White fur sprouts from her nose, revealing the Yao to be a hare.
Her feet begin to stamp like war drums. The other Yao watch, then look at one another. All of them feeling the pull to join in.

items.speaker: Hare
items.text: The Immortal will grant us longevity!

items.speaker: All Yao
items.text: The Immortal will grant us longevity!

items.speaker: Yao I
items.text: Constables! Run!

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: What?
As they round the mouth of the alley, the parade vanishes as quickly as it appeared. The chanting music fades like smoke in the air.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mayfly? Can you hear me? You were caught in the parade's illusion. I had to lead you away.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I-I'm alright now. Those Yao—they're seeking longevity.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But what they're doing is a risk to our entire community.
Mayfly looks down, her face turning red. Finally deciding something, she stamps her foot.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Paper Heron, thank you for bringing me here. I owe you much, so I don't want to lie anymore. I ...
Paper Heron tilts her head, looking puzzled but relieved.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Lie about what?

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: You know my true form is a tuft of reed. I'm a Yao, just like the others in the parade.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: In truth, the reason I came all this way is to seek the Method of Longevity. I lied because, well, I feared you'd hate me. I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But I don't want to hurt anyone. I just wanna live longer. Even a little would do.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hush. You'll hear no judgment from me. Only, I don't understand.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: You risked a lifetime of confinement on a rumor. Is longevity really so important to you?
She goes quiet for a moment, then looks down.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Remember the travelers we met on the way here? Human or Yao, all sought the Method of Longevity.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: But you're different. You care more for the small joys in life, like that sweet olive cake we shared.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: It's almost as if you don't care about how long you'll live at all.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Ah ...

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: I'm not so unlike you. I suppose I'm just curious about everything.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: We're already here. Why hurry? If we'd missed that cake, we'd have regretted it for the rest of our lives.
Paper Heron scratches her head as she tries to explain; words rest on her tongue, but they feel, like her, suddenly out of place.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: *sigh* You win.
She brushes her skirt and sighs.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Sorry, I shouldn't have been so suspicious of you.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Though we study arcanum and can take human shapes, we Yao are still just plants and animals. Even if we look like you, our lives are much shorter.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Reeds like me sprout in spring and wither in winter. My entire life begins and ends in less than a year.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: I know it's foolish to risk so much on a rumor, but it's all I have.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Do you know what I think when the sun sets? Not that the sky is lovely, but that I lost another day. I don't want to live in fear anymore.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: But you spent all you had on that amulet.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: What if the Method of Longevity proves false? You'll have nothing left.
Mayfly smiles, but she lets her eyes stay downcast for a moment before they rise to meet her own.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: Longevity means much more to me than you, Heron. When the winter ends, you will see the spring, and I won't.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: If the Method is true, it will change everything. I have to take the chance, no matter the cost.

items.speaker: Mayfly
items.text: And as you said yourself, I have nothing left to lose.
They share a long gaze. Paper Heron reads the dark eyes before her. They seem to burn like unsettled coal.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Mayfly ...
The usually free-spirited Daoist is, for a moment, speechless. She intends to speak, but then the unexpected strikes.

items.speaker: Serious Male Voice
items.text: Commander!
The familiar voice comes from around the corner, seizing her train of thought.

items.speaker: Paper Heron
items.text: Hmm?

items.speaker: Cheng Heguang
items.text: Commander, I come with an urgent report.
